document.title: Lion's Python Programming Guidelines (2025) -- Simplified Edition
document.purpose: simplified JSON version, for use by LLM programming agents

purpose: A short, structural rule-set for building simple, readable, castle-style procedural systems.
core_beliefs: Structure should be visible from a distance.
Context carries meaning; names and flags refine it.
Inside the system, assumptions are trusted.
Outside the system, data is normalized before entry.

design_principles.name: Minimal Construction
design_principles.rule: Do not build scaffolding unless it carries real weight.
notes: Avoid abstraction layers that only organize, not transform.
If a thing is used once, let it be local and obvious.

design_principles.name: Soft Modularity
design_principles.rule: Repeat small patterns instead of inventing big structures.
notes: Let similar code look similar, even if duplicated slightly.

design_principles.name: Trusted Interior
notes: No optional fields once data is admitted.
Validation happens at boundaries, not everywhere.

design_principles.name: Castle Gate
design_principles.rule: Normalize all external input before use.

design_principles.name: Separate Validation
notes: Validation functions do not perform work.

state_and_globals.philosophy: Globals are acceptable and often preferable.
rules: Group related scalars into small bundles.
Keep large or volatile data in dedicated containers.
Prefer one canonical global bundle named 'g'.
Third argument is reserved for flags.

flags.purpose: Select behavior without multiplying function names.
rules: Each flag has one meaning everywhere.
Context explains most of the intent.

callbacks.meaning: this is where the outside world enters

internal_helpers.rule: same naming rules, but start with '_'

classes.reflection_rule: Before using a class, ask how to express this procedurally.

acceptable_cases: blocking I/O that cannot be event-driven

rules: outermost structure is list or dict
multi_process_coordination.philosophy: Programs live in an ecosystem, not in isolation.

should_explain: what shape of data it expects

documentation.philosophy: Code should read like a story even without comments.

closing: The goal is not theoretical purity.
The goal is momentum, legibility, and trust in the system.
Good code feels like walking through a familiar city, not navigating a maze.
